solution_overview:
An app studies customer usage of three features: Auto-save (P), Dark mode (Q), and Cloud sync (R). The problem provides a Venn diagram showing the probability of a randomly selected customer falling into each distinct region, including those who use none of the three features.

We denote the events as $P$ (Auto-save), $Q$ (Dark mode), and $R$ (Cloud sync).

The given probabilities for the eight mutually exclusive regions are:
*   $P(P \cap Q^c \cap R^c) = 0.15$ (only P)
*   $P(P^c \cap Q \cap R^c) = 0.10$ (only Q)
*   $P(P^c \cap Q^c \cap R) = 0.08$ (only R)
*   $P(P \cap Q \cap R^c) = 0.06$ (P and Q, not R)
*   $P(P \cap Q^c \cap R) = 0.04$ (P and R, not Q)
*   $P(P^c \cap Q \cap R) = 0.05$ (Q and R, not P)
*   $P(P \cap Q \cap R) = 0.03$ (P, Q, and R)
*   $P(P^c \cap Q^c \cap R^c) = 0.49$ (none of the features)
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

The probability that a customer uses at least one of the three features is the complement of using none of the features. The sum of probabilities for all eight mutually exclusive regions is 1.

$$P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(P^c \cap Q^c \cap R^c)$$

$$P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - 0.49$$

$$P(\text{at least one}) = 0.51$$

The claim is that this probability is greater than $52\%$, or $0.52$. We found $0.51$, so $0.51 \not> 0.52$, and the statement is False.

**B.** → True

The event "exactly two of the three features" corresponds to the union of three mutually exclusive regions: using P and Q but not R ($P \cap Q \cap R^c$), using P and R but not Q ($P \cap Q^c \cap R$), and using Q and R but not P ($P^c \cap Q \cap R$). We sum their probabilities:

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = P(P \cap Q \cap R^c) + P(P \cap Q^c \cap R) + P(P^c \cap Q \cap R)$$

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = 0.06 + 0.04 + 0.05$$

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = 0.15$$

The claim is that this probability equals $15\%$. Since $0.15 = 15\%$, the statement is True.

**C.** → False

The probability that a customer uses Auto-save, given that they use Dark mode or Cloud sync, is a conditional probability $P(P \mid Q \cup R)$. This is defined as $P(P \cap (Q \cup R)) / P(Q \cup R)$.

First, calculate the probability of the conditioning event $Q \cup R$. This is the sum of probabilities of all regions where $Q$ or $R$ (or both) are present:

$$P(Q \cup R) = P(P^c \cap Q \cap R^c) + P(P^c \cap Q^c \cap R) + P(P \cap Q \cap R^c)$$

$$+ P(P \cap Q^c \cap R) + P(P^c \cap Q \cap R) + P(P \cap Q \cap R)$$

$$P(Q \cup R) = 0.10 + 0.08 + 0.06 + 0.04 + 0.05 + 0.03$$

$$P(Q \cup R) = 0.36$$

Next, calculate the probability of the intersection $P \cap (Q \cup R)$. This means using Auto-save ($P$) and also at least one of Dark mode ($Q$) or Cloud sync ($R$). This corresponds to the regions ($P \cap Q \cap R^c$), ($P \cap Q^c \cap R$), and ($P \cap Q \cap R$):

$$P(P \cap (Q \cup R)) = P(P \cap Q \cap R^c) + P(P \cap Q^c \cap R) + P(P \cap Q \cap R)$$

$$P(P \cap (Q \cup R)) = 0.06 + 0.04 + 0.03$$

$$P(P \cap (Q \cup R)) = 0.13$$

Now, compute the conditional probability:

$$P(P \mid Q \cup R) = \frac{P(P \cap (Q \cup R))}{P(Q \cup R)} = \frac{0.13}{0.36}$$

$$P(P \mid Q \cup R) \approx 0.3611$$

The claim is that this probability is greater than $37\%$, or $0.37$. Since $0.3611 \not> 0.37$, the statement is False.

**D.** → True

The event "exactly one of Auto-save and Dark mode" means a customer uses Auto-save but not Dark mode ($P \cap Q^c$), or Dark mode but not Auto-save ($P^c \cap Q$). These are two mutually exclusive events.

The event $P \cap Q^c$ includes customers who use only Auto-save ($P \cap Q^c \cap R^c$) or Auto-save and Cloud sync ($P \cap Q^c \cap R$):

$$P(P \cap Q^c) = P(P \cap Q^c \cap R^c) + P(P \cap Q^c \cap R)$$

$$P(P \cap Q^c) = 0.15 + 0.04 = 0.19$$

The event $P^c \cap Q$ includes customers who use only Dark mode ($P^c \cap Q \cap R^c$) or Dark mode and Cloud sync ($P^c \cap Q \cap R$):

$$P(P^c \cap Q) = P(P^c \cap Q \cap R^c) + P(P^c \cap Q \cap R)$$

$$P(P^c \cap Q) = 0.10 + 0.05 = 0.15$$

To find the probability of using exactly one of Auto-save and Dark mode, we sum these two probabilities:

$$P(\text{exactly one of P and Q}) = P(P \cap Q^c) + P(P^c \cap Q)$$

$$P(\text{exactly one of P and Q}) = 0.19 + 0.15$$

$$P(\text{exactly one of P and Q}) = 0.34$$

The claim is that this probability is greater than $32\%$, or $0.32$. Since $0.34 > 0.32$, the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The probability that a customer uses all three features is given directly by the region $P \cap Q \cap R$:

$$P(\text{all three}) = P(P \cap Q \cap R) = 0.03$$

The probability that a customer uses exactly two features was calculated in Statement B:

$$P(\text{exactly two}) = 0.15$$

The claim compares $P(\text{all three})$ with one-quarter of $P(\text{exactly two})$. We calculate the comparison value:

$$\frac{1}{4} \times P(\text{exactly two}) = \frac{1}{4} \times 0.15$$

$$\frac{1}{4} \times P(\text{exactly two}) = 0.0375$$

Comparing the probability of using all three features, $0.03$, with $0.0375$, we find that $0.03 < 0.0375$, so the statement is True.
